# Introduction

In this notebook we explain how we process the data for the ICPhS paper **Is gesture-speech physics at work in rhythmic pointing? Evidence from Polish counting-out rhymes**

# Detailed explanation of the study and the type of data and variables

Eleven native speakers (three male) of Polish were asked to perform six counting-out rhymes in two different movement conditions and one still condition. The movement conditions involved the counting-out movement with the left or the right hand, and the still condition involved reading the rhyme without any movement. All speakers were right-handed. Additionally, in the movement conditions, speakers were asked to repeat the rhyme with enhanced speed, resulting in another condition. 

Altogether, these sum up to five conditions:

* left hand normal speed
* left hand fast speed
* right hand normal speed
* right hand fast speed
* reading

The order of the blocks was the same for all participants (reading, natural, fast), but the order of counting-out rhymes was randomized as well as whether they began with the dominant or non-dominant hand.

In all of those conditions, the participants performed six counting-out rhymes, the order of which was randomized across participants (cf. rhyme_order.xlsx or columns 6:11 in info.xlsx).

The participants were asked to perform each rhyme with a confederate teddy bear placed in front of them. For each condition, the participants were standing.

# Processing the audio into time series

## Amplitude envelope extraction
```{r extract_amplitude envelope, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

# you can check out: https://wimpouw.github.io/EnvisionBootcamp2021/extract_AmplitudeEnvelope_Rmarkdown.html

overwrite <- FALSE # do not overwrite existing files

#list of the wav's                                                                    
list_wavs <- list.files(folderaudio, pattern = ".wav") 

# processsing settings
resample_rate <- 200 # Hz
smoothing <- 5 # 5Hz low pass hanning (the lower the value the more smooth)


##################### main function to extract smoothed envelope ###############################

amplitude_envelope.extract <- function(locationsound, smoothingHz, resampledHz)
{
  #read the sound file into R
  snd <- rPraat::snd.read(locationsound)
  #apply the hilbert on the signal
  hilb <- seewave::hilbert(snd$sig, f = snd$fs, fftw =FALSE)
  #apply complex modulus
  env <- as.vector(abs(hilb))
  #smooth with a hanning window
  env_smoothed <- dplR::hanning(x= env, n = snd$fs/smoothingHz)
  #set undeterminable at beginning and end NA's to 0
  env_smoothed[is.na(env_smoothed)] <- 0
  #resample settings at desired sampling rate
  f <- approxfun(1:(snd$duration*snd$fs),env_smoothed)
  #resample apply
  downsampled <- f(seq(from=0,to=snd$duration*snd$fs,by=snd$fs/resampledHz))
  #let function return the downsampled smoothed amplitude envelope
  return(downsampled[!is.na(downsampled)])
}

#loop through soundfile locations
for(wav in list_wavs)
  {
   #do not run this when these files are already generated
  if((!file.exists(paste0(dataworkspace, substr(wav, 1, nchar(wav)-4), "_ENV", ".csv"))) & (overwrite!=TRUE))
  {
  #location of the current sound file in the loop  
  locsound <- paste0(folderaudio, wav)
  #get the amplitude envelope at location, 5Hz Hanning, 100Hz sampling
  env <- amplitude_envelope.extract(locsound, smoothing, resample_rate)
  #make a time vector based on sampling rate (1000/Hz)
  time_ms <- seq(1000/resample_rate, length(env)*(1000/resample_rate), by = 1000/resample_rate)
  #bind into data frame
  ENV <- cbind.data.frame(time_ms, env)
  #save it to a folder
  write.csv(ENV, file = paste0(paste0(dataworkspace, substr(wav, 1, nchar(wav)-4), "_ENV", ".csv")),row.names=FALSE) 
  }
}
```

## F0 Extraction
```{r extractF0, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}

#for info see here https://osf.io/m43qy
#this script automatically assesses F0 traces from audio using WRASSP. It also needs a META data_file containing gender information so as to set F0 ranges.
# Function extracts F0 traces from wav, given gender info, at a particular sampling frequency
# algorithm is based on K. Schaefer-Vincent periodicity detection
#FOR INFO ABOUT WRASSP SEE https://ips-lmu.github.io/The-EMU-SDMS-Manual/chap-wrassp.html

#SET DATA READING AND WRITING LOCATIONS
list_wavs <- list.files(paste0(folderaudio), pattern = ".wav")
META <- read_excel(paste0(folderaudio, "/info.xlsx"))
META$gender <- ifelse(META$sex=='female', 'f', 'm')

#processsing settings
resample_rate <- 200 #Hz

# do we want to overwrite files?
overwrite <- FALSE

################### function to extract F0 ############################

F0.extract <- function(locationsound, gender_fm, resampledHz)
{
  if(gender_fm == 'f'){ ranges <- c(100, 450)} # ranges for females and males (data-driven decision)
  if(gender_fm == 'm'){ ranges <- c(70, 300)}

  minF0   <- ranges[1] 
  maxF0   <- ranges[2]

  F0     <- wrassp::ksvF0(locationsound, windowShift=1000/resampledHz, toFile = FALSE, maxF = maxF0, minF = minF0) 
  
  #extract F0 info and save into object
  
  F0_vec <- F0$F0[,1]                                                                        #only save F0 trace
  F0_time <- seq(from = attributes(F0)$startTime*1000,                                       #make time vector
                 to = attributes(F0)$endRecord[1]*(1000/attributes(F0)$sampleRate), 
                 by = 1000/attributes(F0)$sampleRate )
  F0_df <- cbind.data.frame(round(F0_time), F0_vec) #save time and F0 trace into one object
  return( F0_df )
}

#loop through the folder containing audio (wav files) and extract F0
for(wav in list_wavs)
  {

    #do not run this when these files are already generated
    if((!file.exists(paste0(dataworkspace, str_sub(wav, end = -5), "_F0.csv"))) | (overwrite==TRUE))
    {
    #take gender info
    print(wav)
    PP <- readr::parse_number(wav) #what is the participant number as indicated by the filename of the audio
    gender <- META$gender[META$VP==PP] #save the gender from META based on the participantnumber
    locsound <- paste0(folderaudio, wav)                      #where is the soundfile
    F0_vec <- F0.extract(locsound, gender, resample_rate)                      #APPLY MAIN FUNCTION
    colnames(F0_vec) <- c("time_ms", "F0")
    write.csv(F0_vec, file = paste0(dataworkspace, str_sub(wav, end = -5), "_F0.csv"),row.names=FALSE) #WRITE TO A FILE AND SAVE
    }
  }
```

## Other functions
```{r functions to be used, echo = TRUE}

################### load.in.even function##################

#this function loads into a time series an annotation dataframe with columns (begintime, endtime, annotation)
load.in.event <- function(time_original, anno)
{
  output <- rep(NA, length(time_original))
  for(i in 1:length(anno[,1])) #loop through each annotation event
  {
    #print(anno[i,3]) #you can print the value to check if this is running correctly
    output <- ifelse((time_original >= anno[i,1] & time_original <= anno[i,2]), as.character(anno[i,3]), output)
  }
  return(output)
}

############# load.in.anno function ############################

load.in.anno_num <- function(time_original, anno)
{
  output <- rep(NA, length(time_original))
  for(i in 1:length(anno[,1])) #loop through each annotation event
  {
    #print(anno[i,3]) #you can print the value to check if this is running correctly
    output <- ifelse((time_original >= anno[i,1] & time_original <= anno[i,2]), as.character(anno[i,4]), output)
  }
  return(output)
}

########################## gesture phases function ##############################################

########################## Corrigendum note ####################################################

# Here we corrected the function for detecting phases. Previously, it incorrectly assigned gesture phase, as the
# number increased after every detected peak, even if the direction of the movement didn't change. We corrected it
# such that it only assigns new gesture phase number if also the direction of the movement changed

## this function automatically detect phases in gesture movement

getphases.it <- function(time, mvmnt, syll) {
  
    # Convert the syllable_num column to numeric
  syll <- as.numeric(as.character(syll))

  # Find the minimum and maximum times for syllable_num 2 and the last unique value in syllable_num, respectively (first and last syllable in each rhyme is a pause)
  minsyll <- min(time[syll==2])
  maxsyll <- max(time[syll==(length(unique(syll))-1)])

  # Create a speech column that indicates whether there is ongoing speech or not
  speech <- "no on speech"
  speech[time >= minsyll & time <= maxsyll]  <- "ongoing speech"

  # Create column for peaks
  peaks_tbs <- rep(NA, length(mvmnt))
  # Centering the mvmnt values so forward is + and backward -
  centered_mvmnt <- mvmnt - mean(mvmnt) 
  # Finding peaks of absolutized mvmnt (for both backward and forward mvmnt)
  allpeaks <- findpeaks(abs(centered_mvmnt))[,2] 
  peaks_tbs[allpeaks] <- mvmnt[allpeaks] # put those peaks into peak-column
  peaks_tbs[!is.na(peaks_tbs)] <- ifelse(centered_mvmnt[allpeaks] > 0, 'start_backward', 'start_forward') #if values are -, it's start of forward mvmnt, if +, start of the backward

  # Create the annotation data frame with the begin and end times for each gesture phase
  begintime <- time[allpeaks[1:length(allpeaks)-1]] #remove the last value
  endtime <-  time[allpeaks[-1]] #remove the first value
  anno <-  ifelse(peaks_tbs[allpeaks[1:length(allpeaks)-1]]=='start_backward', 'forward_movement','backward_movement') # annotation of mvmnt direction
  anno2 <-  cumsum(c(TRUE, anno[-1] != anno[-length(anno)])) # annotation of gesture phases (by numbers; consecutive segments with same direction share a number)
  gesturephas <- cbind.data.frame(begintime, endtime, anno) # gp by direction
  gesturephas2 <- cbind.data.frame(begintime, endtime, anno2) # gp by number
  
  #get it ready to use our function again to load annotations into a time series
  gesture_phases <- load.in.event(time, gesturephas)
  gesture_phases2 <- load.in.event(time, gesturephas2)
  
  return(cbind(gesture_phases,gesture_phases2))
}
```

## Merging motion tracking 
```{r merginstuff, echo = TRUE}

# we will now merge F0, envelope, textgrids with right hand data (200 Hz sampling frequency)

#first give the list of files for which we have envelopes
envelopedata <- list.files(dataworkspace, pattern = '*.ENV.csv')

############# butter filter ###############
butter.it <- function(x, samplingrate = 200, order=2, lowpasscutoff=30)
{bf <- butter(order,lowpasscutoff/samplingrate, type="low") #normalized frequency
x <<- as.numeric(signal::filtfilt(bf, x))} #apply forwards and backwards using filtfilt

############### merging ###################

#loop through them and merge
for(d in envelopedata)
{
   #d <- envelopedata[1] # for when you want to test
   trial <- str_remove(d, '_ENV.csv')
   lefttrue <- grepl('Left', d, fixed = TRUE) #does it contain left (than it is a Left handed trial)
   kside <- ifelse(lefttrue, '_L', '_R')  #check which hand we need

   #read envelope
   env <- read.csv(paste0(dataworkspace, '/', d))
   #read F0
   F0 <- read.csv(paste0(dataworkspace, '/', trial, '_F0.csv'))
   #read textgrid and prepare them for reading into the time series
   fname <- paste0(folderaudio, trial, '.TextGrid')
   
   if(file.exists(fname))
   {
   #prepare textgrids
   txtgrds <- readtextgrid::read_textgrid(fname)
   txtgrds_syl <- txtgrds[txtgrds$tier_name=='SYL',]
   xmin <- round(txtgrds_syl$xmin*1000)
   ymin <- round(txtgrds_syl$xmax*1000)
   anno1 <- txtgrds_syl$text
   anno_num <- txtgrds_syl$annotation_num
   annotation <- cbind.data.frame(xmin,ymin,anno1,anno_num) #we end up with a file that we can use in our read annotation function
   check1 <- file.exists(paste0(foldermotion,  trial,kside, 'FING.csv'))
   check2 <- file.exists(paste0(foldermotion,  trial,kside, 'HAND.csv'))

   #get ready for preprocessing speech or or speech and motion
   lesen <- grepl("Lesen", d, fixed = TRUE) # check if it contains Lesen
   
   ######## merging lesen files #################
   if(lesen) #if it is a lesen condition there is no movement so well fill with empties
   {
     ac_merged     <- merge(x=env, y = F0, by.x = "time_ms", by.y = "time_ms", all=TRUE)
     ac_merged$env <-  na.approx(ac_merged$env, x = ac_merged$time_ms,
na.rm=FALSE)
     ac_merged <- ac_merged[(!is.na(ac_merged$F0)),]
     ac_merged <- na.trim(ac_merged) #also remove trailing Na's
     
     # make some empty variables
     ac_merged$x_fing <- ac_merged$y_fing <- ac_merged$z_fing <- ac_merged$x_wrist <- ac_merged$y_wrist <- ac_merged$z_wrist <- ac_merged$x_elb <-
     ac_merged$y_elb <- ac_merged$z_elb <- ac_merged$speed_fing <- ac_merged$speed_wrist <- ac_merged$speed_elb <- ac_merged$acc_fing <- ac_merged$acc_wrist <-
     ac_merged$acc_elb <- ac_merged$gesture_phases <- ac_merged$movementdirection<- NA
     #read in textgrid info
     ac_merged$syllable <- load.in.event(time_original = ac_merged$time_ms, anno = annotation) #apply function
     ac_merged$syllable_num <- load.in.anno_num(time_original = ac_merged$time_ms, anno = annotation) #apply function
     #add some info for analyses
     ac_merged$participant <- readr::parse_number(sub("\\_.*", "", trial))
     ac_merged$hand <- NA
     ac_merged$speed_condition <- ifelse(grepl("fast", trial), "fast",
"normal")
       # look for last five characters and make new column rhyme
     ac_merged$rhyme <- parse_number(str_sub(trial,-5,-1))
     ac_merged$rhyme <- as.factor(ac_merged$rhyme)
     ac_merged$condition_speech <- "lesen"
      
     ################ adding rhyme name info ##################
     # loop over the rows of the df data frame 
     for (i in 1:nrow(ac_merged)) {
       # get the participant and rhyme values for the current row
       participant <- as.character(ac_merged[i, "participant"])
       rhyme <- as.character(ac_merged[i, "rhyme"])

       # loop over the matching rows of the info data frame

na.rm=FALSE)

   colnames(mov_merged) <- c('time_ms', movementvariables)

   #movement columns
   #merge movements and acoustics
   mac_merged     <- merge(x=ac_merged, y = mov_merged, by.x = "time_ms", by.y = "time_ms", all=TRUE)
   mac_merged[,movementvariables] <-
apply(mac_merged[,movementvariables], 2, FUN = function(y) na.approx(y, x = mac_merged$time_ms, na.rm=FALSE))
   mac_merged <- mac_merged[(!is.na(mac_merged$F0)),]
   mac_merged <- na.trim(mac_merged) #also remove trailing Na's

apply(mac_merged[,movementvariables], 2, FUN = function(y) butter.it(x=y))
   #add 3D speed and 3D acceleration)
   mac_merged$speed_fing  <- butter.it(c(0,sqrt(diff(mac_merged$x_fing
)^2+diff(mac_merged$y_fing)^2+diff(mac_merged$z_fing)^2)))

   mac_merged$acc_wrist <- butter.it(c(0, diff(mac_merged$speed_wrist)))
   mac_merged$acc_elb  <- butter.it(c(0, diff(mac_merged$speed_elb )))
     #to remove the edge effect, we will not consider the first values
   mac_merged[c(1:50, (nrow(mac_merged)-50):nrow(mac_merged)),] <- NA
   mac_merged <- na.trim(mac_merged)

"normal")
     # look for last five characters and make new column rhyme

  ############# add rhyme name info ##################
  # loop over the rows of the df data frame 
     for (i in 1:nrow(mac_merged)) {

 ######## correction of syllables ################
```
